title: fix(scripts): hold check-engine-double-contract --write to the same population floor as the reporting run
body:
Clause-②: no

Closes #17117

#17099 gave `check-engine-double-contract` a **population floor** so a run that read almost
nothing REFUSES instead of reporting on the fraction it reached. That floor was spelled inline
in `report()`, and `--write` is a **sibling branch of the same dispatch chain** — it re-scanned
and rewrote both ledgers with nothing in front of it. **The floor protected the reader and left
the writer free to destroy the thing being protected.**

## What changed

One shared `refusePopulationFloor()` is now the only thing in the file that turns a fallen floor
into an exit. `report()` and `writeLedger()` both call it; `writeLedger()` calls it **before the
first `writeFileSync`**, so a refused regeneration leaves the ledgers that were already on disk
and says so.

**Not a fourth copy** — see the ordering note below. `populationFloorProblem` stays the only
decider; the file goes from one inline refusal to one helper with two call sites. `--census`
deliberately stays out: it reaches no verdict and writes nothing (#9747's ruling), so it has
nothing to destroy; the day it writes or decides anything it joins the list rather than growing a
third refusal.

The floor is over the **derived population** and never over a ledger's size, so the bootstrap both
ledger readers document still holds: a fresh checkout with the artifacts absent walks the whole
tree, clears all four counts, and writes them.

## Verdict on today's ledger — CORRECT, nothing restored

Triage pinned this as the prerequisite: if a previous `--write` already baked an under-collected
population, the pin is wrong today and restoring it is part of the fix. It is not wrong.

Measured on the unmodified tree at the branch point (`66e34d14d9`), before any edit:

```
check-engine-double-contract: OK — 875 pinned, 133 in the DEBT ledger, 3 exempt.
check-engine-double-contract: 800 (file, verb) row(s) held by the RETAINED ledger
  provenance — testFiles/productionFiles/discoveredFiles/pinnedRows: this run 3685/2732/932/800
  · floors 2800/2000/700/600 · derived from 3503/2596/911/779 measured on 854639b311
  (+182/+136/+21/+21 vs the record)
```

Three legs, and the first is decisive rather than circumstantial:

1. **The reporting run reconciles the ledger against the LIVE census in both directions** and
   exits 0. The growth direction errors once per row the census finds and the ledger does not; the
   loss direction errors once per row the ledger records and the scan no longer sees. A green run
   therefore means the ledger's set **equals** today's census row for row — a baked-down ledger
   could not produce it. This is a measurement of the ledger, not an inference about its history.
2. **Every population count is above its floor and above the record** it was derived from
   (+182/+136/+21/+21). A collapsed scan is not what produced this ledger.
3. **The ledger's row count across the 25 most recent commits that touched it** climbs 765 → 800
   with one legitimate 6-row dip (782 → 776 on 2026-09-10). No collapse anywhere in that window.
   ⚠️ This checkout is shallow, so leg 3 is a positive reading over the window it holds and is
   **not** an absence claim over all time; legs 1 and 2 do not depend on history at all.

⇒ **Nothing was restored, because nothing needed restoring.** The ledgers are byte-identical to
`origin/main` in this PR — the diff is one file.

## Positive control — `--write` refuses instead of writing a shrunken ledger

Acceptance ⭐: without this, floor-added and floor-not-added look identical. Run from the committed
state; the under-collection is the same one-package collapse the POPULATION FLOORS header was
measured on (`SCAN_ROOTS` restricted to `packages/mcp`).

**Leg A — floor wired, scan restricted.** `--write` exits **2** (`EXIT_POPULATION_REFUSED`):

```
check-engine-double-contract REFUSES — measured only 31 test file(s) offered by the discovery
walk, below the floor of 2800 (3503 on 854639b311).
  ⛔ NOTHING WAS WRITTEN. The pinned and seam ledgers on disk are the ones that were already
  there — a regeneration from this scan would have recorded the collapse as the new population.

  pinned ledger after: 5f8d55bf…  (HEAD 5f8d55bf…)   ✓ BYTE-IDENTICAL
  seam   ledger after: 984cd43a…  (HEAD 984cd43a…)   ✓ BYTE-IDENTICAL
```

**Leg B — ablation, the writer's floor call removed, same restricted scan.** `--write` exits **0**
and rewrites both ledgers:

```
  gate hash moved f413d458… -> 18fbbf78…   ✓ the ablation is on disk
  --write exit=0
  pinned ledger after: 993281c0…  (HEAD 5f8d55bf…)   ✓ REWRITTEN
  shrunken ledger rows: 15        (was 800)
  shrunken seam rows:    2        (was 6)
```

15 pinned rows where the tree has 800 — the exact collapse #17099's dev measured and the card was
filed on. Leg B is what makes Leg A evidence rather than a tautology.

**Restore settled by bytes, ⛔ never by an exit code** (the container's `trap` can silently not
fire — #17875; `trap` is present as a crash-path convenience only and is not the proof):

```
  gate   eee738f3… vs HEAD eee738f3…
  pinned 5f8d55bf… vs HEAD 5f8d55bf…
  seam   984cd43a… vs HEAD 984cd43a…
  ✓ git diff HEAD is EMPTY
```

An empty `git hash-object` output is treated as FAILURE, not as "nothing to compare", and the
mutation legs prove they landed by counting the anchor text before and after — an editor's exit
code is not on-disk evidence.

## Order taken, and the shape — re-stated because triage asked

**This card first, #17118 not touched**, per the PM's ruling. #17118 records that the floor
mechanism exists three times under two spellings across the gate family.

**This implementation is not a fourth copy of the floor.** It adds no new floor anywhere: it
de-duplicates *within* this file, going from one inline refusal to one helper invoked from two
branches. Net copies of the floor in the tree are unchanged. A self-test case asserts the shape
directly — **exactly one place in this file turns a fallen floor into an exit** — so a future
branch that grew its own refusal reds rather than passing.

⇒ **This leaves #17118 strictly easier, not harder**: its consolidation now re-points one helper in
this file instead of two inline blocks. I do **not** judge that the shared helper had to land
first, and I did not widen.

## Self-test — the wiring, not the decider

The 23 existing floor cases all passed while `--write` never called the floor. That is the shape of
the defect: driving a pure decider cannot say which branches reach it. A new battery
(`Every branch that SCANS routes through the floor (#17117)`, 6 cases) reads this file's own
source — same instrument as the existing `PROVENANCE — the pass path in report() still prints it`
case — and pins that both branches route through the helper, that the write call precedes the first
`writeFileSync`, and that exactly one place exits on a fallen floor. A control case asserts the body
reader finds a body at all, so the four scoped assertions cannot pass vacuously.

## Reverse-read — including the zeros

*What in the tree does this change make false?*

- **Re-judged in place, ⛔ not deleted:** the POPULATION FLOORS header's one-package reproduction
  recipe. Its `--write` step now meets a refusal. The reading it was taken to establish is
  unchanged and is still why the floors exist; the note says which half is history and which half
  still holds.
- **The gate's own self-test verdict sentence** now names the routing clause it covers.

*What states that the floor applies only to the reporting run?* **ZERO outside the gate.**
`git grep` for the scope phrasing across the tree returns one unrelated hit in
`check-undeclared-dep-imports.mjs` (its own floors' provenance wording). The only prose that carried
the scope was inside this gate, and both places are handled above.

*What describes this ledger's population?* **ZERO prose statements of its size.** The only external
mentions are three per-file comments
(`plugin-security/src/permission-set-drift.test.ts`, `permission-set-overlay-discard.test.ts`,
`runtime/src/standalone-stack-seeder-declaration-copy.test.ts`) that each describe **their own row**,
not the population — unaffected. The `800` and `875` figures are computed at runtime, never written
into prose.

*Reverse direction — anything that was false and is now true?* The two ledger `$comment` strings are
the only places outside the gate naming `--write` ("Regenerate with … ; never hand-edit"). They were
true before and remain true: the command is unchanged, it now refuses on a collapsed scan. Both
files are byte-identical in this PR.

## Verification

All against `e7427b155c`, the final commit.

- `pnpm check:engine-double-contract` — **exit 0**, `OK — 875 pinned, 133 in the DEBT ledger,
  3 exempt`, provenance `3685/2732/932/800`.
- **32 of 32** derived gate families run, all exit 0.
  `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --ran …` →
  `✓ 32 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 32 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 32
  recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)`.
- `node scripts/check-commit-card-trailers.mjs --range origin/main..HEAD` — exit 0.
- Control-character self-scan over the edited file — `grep` exit 1 (clean), captured before any pipe.
- Exit codes read from each gate's own printed verdict line with `$?` captured before any pipe,
  ⛔ never through one.

Repo-wide scans (`pnpm lint` and the 51 artifact-roster, 11 wide-population, 14 pending-changeset
families and the path-scheduled CI job the derivation names) are **CI's runs, declared not run
locally** — they are outside the derived set by that tool's own accounting.

## Changeset — SKIP, measured

`.changeset` skipped and the **`skip-changeset` label** applied (a label, not a body sentence).

Measured rather than assumed: the changed path lies inside **0** of the repo's **70** published
package directories, and the repo root package is `private: true`. Positive control —
`packages/objectql/src/engine-delete-dispatch.ts` resolves into exactly one published package whose
`files[]` is `["dist","README.md","CHANGELOG.md"]`, so the instrument does find a published file when
one exists. Nothing any package ships moves.

## 验收备注

- `--census` (the third sibling branch) is left alone deliberately, and the reason is in the code:
  it reaches no verdict and changes no exit code, so it is a reporter with nothing to destroy. Noted
  in the helper's doc comment as the criterion for when it would join.
- Triage recorded that `check-type-check-coverage`'s `--re-measure` / `--lower` branches may hold the
  same shape and that the ordering there was **not** established. I did not widen into it; it is
  #17118's neighbourhood and the PM ruled against widening.
